Decision gate (soundness): scripts/check_docs_ownership.py, scripts/check_comment_policy.py and scripts/comment_syntax.py are soundness paths; arm only on the reviewer's success verdict for the current head.

description:
Source: a retrospective over 25 agent sessions (2026-10-18 to 2026-11-11), followed by an adversarial re-check of each claim against origin/develop 4835f5a537.

Problem. Three failures gave no next step, so sessions read checker source to find it.
(1) tests/unit/scripts/test_inert_paths.py::test_checked_in_readers_match_the_rebuilt_index is a bare assert. The fix command, `_project/scripts/inert_paths.py --regenerate-readers`, appears only in docs/internal/review-v2.md. One session spent about 10 calls and 8 minutes after a CI failure.
(2) scripts/check_docs_ownership.py raises 'tracked docs coverage mismatch: missing=[...]' without naming quality/docs-ownership.json or the owner value to add. Two sessions grepped for a sibling doc to find the manifest.
(3) A comment-policy `payload-error` for a registered fixture whose payload changed prints neither the computed digest nor a pointer to docs/internal/comment-policy.md. One session re-read the checker four times (about 30 calls) and once concluded wrongly that the rebind had failed.

Change. (1) Give the assert a message naming the regeneration command. (2) Extend the ownership error to name the manifest and say that a new core doc is registered as `core-only`. (3) Where a payload-error concerns a registered fixture with a different payload, include the computed `sha256:` digest and the doc path in the finding text, and state that `make comment-policy-check` ignores same-commit fixtures.

Non-goals. No change to what any check accepts or rejects. The worktree ownership refusal already prints the takeover command (scripts/worktree_lifecycle_metadata.py) and is not changed.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone, and pass absolute worktree paths to every file tool; stage paths explicitly, never git add -A; no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); heavy work only via make heavy-run, never forcing admission or skipping the test lock; never bypass a required check, ruleset, hold label or review gate, and never post a stand-in; change only the files this item names, and report anything else as noticed-but-not-touched; re-read every cited file on current origin/develop before editing, because the line numbers here are hints from 2026-11-11 (origin/develop 4835f5a537); close at a merged PR (make pr-open, make pr-arm), and finish this item only after the merge is observed.
